instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Rub 1 tbsp of the oil over a rimmed baking sheet.
Mince 4 of the garlic cloves and the shallot as finely as you can. Add them to a large bowl with the pork, rice flour, cornstarch, honey, 2 tbsp of the fish sauce and the five-spice.
Mix with your hands for 2 minutes, until the meat looks sticky and holds together in one mass. Don't skip this. It's what makes the pork logs springy.
Wet your hands and shape the meat into 12 short logs, each about 3 inches long and 3/4 inch thick. Set them on the oiled sheet with a little space between them.
Bake for 8 minutes. Turn each log over, brush with the remaining 1 tbsp oil, and bake for 8 minutes. Turn the oven to broil and cook for 2 minutes, until the tops are browned in spots.

You're cooking the pork to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when there's no pink left and the juices run clear. Let them rest for 3 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the dipping sauce. Mince the remaining 2 garlic cloves. Stir them in a small bowl with the sugar, 3 tbsp of the fish sauce, the vinegar, the juice of the lime and 1/4 cup warm water until the sugar dissolves.
Put the vermicelli in a heatproof bowl and cover with just-boiled water. Let it stand for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Cut the cucumber into thin sticks, separate the lettuce leaves, and pick the mint and basil leaves.

Fill a wide shallow dish with warm water. Dip one rice paper for about 10 seconds, until it just turns soft, and lay it flat on a plate. Near the bottom edge, set a lettuce leaf, a small handful of noodles, a few cucumber sticks, some herbs and 1 of the cooked logs. Fold in the sides, roll it up tight, and repeat with the rest.

To pack for lunch, keep the pork logs, noodles, vegetables, herbs and sauce in separate containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Roll them the same morning. The pork can be eaten cold or reheated for 30 seconds in the microwave.
method_notes: The sources agree on a seasoned pork paste with rice powder, fish sauce, five-spice and a sweetener, shaped and grilled until browned, then eaten in rice paper with herbs and noodles. SideChef (the lead, 4.0 from 2 ratings) gives the ratios, 1 lb of pork to 2 tbsp each of rice powder and cornstarch, 3 tbsp honey and 2 tbsp fish sauce, while Runaway Rice supplies the oven method and Vicky Pham confirms the long mixing. This version skips the bacon, the cooking wine and the 1 hour chill, and uses plain rice flour for roasted rice powder, to keep it a lunch you can make in under 40 minutes. The dipping sauce is the standard nuoc cham, and all the heat is left out.
